To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the stability of newly formed hybrids can be increased by supplementing the medium with human serum.

human hybridomas can be obtained with a frequency of 0.5-1.5 x 10(-5) by using a modified human hybridoma fusion protocol and that the viability of the newly generated hybrids can be increased by the use of human serum.

the generation and stability (in vitro) of stable IgG secreTING HYBRIDOMAS is significantly improved by using fusion partners with an increased human genome content and a human serum supplemented culture medium.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the generation of a stable and efficient human hybridoma system.
the generation of human hybridomas and the improvement of the stability of these cells.
the development of a novel hybridoma technology which allows for the generation and long-term cultivation of human hybridomas in a human serum supplemented culture system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the use of a human serum containing culture medium and the generation of new fusion lines with a high human DNA content are essential for the successful establishment of human hybridoma clones secreting human IgG antibodies.
the generation of stable antibody secreting hybridoma clones is possible with the use of human serum supplemented medium.
the use of human serum in the culture medium is essential to generate stable human hybridoma cells secreting IgG antibodies.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the use of human serum as a culture supplement in combination with a modified fusion protocol and the use of fusion lines with an elevated human DNA content allows the generation of human IgG secreting hybridomas with an efficiency comparable that of the generation IgM and IgG secreting hybrids.
the generation of stable IgG secretering hybridomas requires the application of human serum supplemented culture medium and the generation of fusion lines with increased human DNA content.

the generation of stable antibody secreting human hybridomas can be improved by the use of fusion lines with a higher human DNA content, the application of human serum supplemented medium and the use of a lymphoblastoid fusion partner.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the generation of stable IgG secretering human hybridomas requires a high frequency of hybridoma formation, and that this can be achieved in a culture system that mimics the natural environment of the human B cell.
the stability of hybridomas is dependent on the culture system used and that the use of serum is necessary for the growth and maintenance of stable IgG secreted hybridomas.
human IgG hybridomas may be obtained by somatic cell hybridizations and that the generation of stable IgG hybridomas can be achieved by supplementing the growth medium with human serum.
